I'll think through my year on the farm before I write down the numbers.

**My reasoning:**

I have 20 mu of land, and like most people around here I do wheat-maize every year. Both my wife and I work the land, and my older son sends some money back from the city, so I'm not too short on cash — but I still count every yuan on fertilizer. 20 mu is not small, and I can't afford big mistakes on either crop.

My wheat is already in the ground since last October. I planted Jimai 22 again — it's the variety the agro-dealer in town keeps pushing and my neighbor Old Wang got over 500 kg/mu with it last year, so I follow. At planting I put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu as base, plus 15 kg of diammonium phosphate. That gives me roughly 12 kg N at the base. At green-up and jointing I will topdress urea — about 20 kg urea per mu total, split in two applications. So altogether around 21 kg N per mu, 8 kg P2O5, 6 kg K2O. I'd rather put a little extra N than watch the leaves go yellow at jointing. I will irrigate 4 times with my well — winter water before the freeze (already done), then green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Pesticide I'll spray maybe 3 times: one for weeds in spring, one for aphids and red spider mites, and one mixed spray for powdery mildew and aphids at heading. I plough-till before wheat planting because the stubble is heavy.

For the summer maize after wheat harvest in June, I'll do no-till direct seeding into the wheat stubble — everyone in the village does it this way now, saves labor and time, and the maize still grows well. I'll buy Zhengdan 958 seed — it's reliable, my neighbors have grown it for years. I put the base fertilizer in the seeder furrow, about 40 kg of 15-15-15 compound per mu, then topdress 25 kg urea per mu at the big-flare stage. That's about 18 kg N per mu, but maize is hungry so I usually give a bit more. Around 6 kg P and 6 kg K. I irrigate the maize once right after sowing to get even emergence, and once more at tasseling if the rain doesn't come. Pesticide twice — one for armyworm and corn borer early, one at tasseling. Last year I got about 580 kg/mu of maize, so I expect similar this year.

If prices of urea go up much more, I will cut the maize topdressing by 5 kg — but I won't touch the wheat rates, wheat is my secure crop.
